minutes.headline: Planning Board continued the Arrow Estates remand hearing to May 13 and voted not to recommend Article 40.
minutes.summary: The board opened the remand hearing on the Arrow Estates subdivisions, now nine plans after the court settlement. Members, abutters and residents raised drainage, traffic, schools, blasting and the form of the town forest access strip, and the applicant took homework items. The board then closed the continued hearing on citizen petition Article 40 and voted not to recommend approval.

public_comment.topic: Asked about number of homes, town forest parking and access, bus service, road condition and drainage on Howard Street, road acceptance, staged construction, and school impact.
Wanted easement versus conveyance clarified and asked whether each lot needs a Title 5 septic system.
Abutter concerned about drainage, wells and septic, open space buffers near existing homes, and whether the layout is final.
Asked about bedroom counts and urged negotiating infrastructure improvements rather than land transfers, noting 44 acres leave the tax rolls.
Wanted a deeded strip rather than an easement, asked whether road acceptance is mandatory, and asked how the board will stop subdivision segmenting.
Questioned the old traffic study, school growth, drainage, ledge and blasting.
Asked about moving the farm access road at a blind corner.
Suggested widening and striping Howard Street and improving sight lines at the entrance.
Asked whether the project could be split among several developers and how drainage and retention would be assured.
Said special permit issues belong with the Board of Selectmen but Article 40 should be debated at Town Meeting.
Clarified that a separate special event license article exists, said the applicant is stuck between three boards, and asked for guidance.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board voted not to recommend approval of citizen petition Article 40 after closing its hearing on it.
The board continued the Arrow Estates remand hearing, now covering nine subdivision plans, to May 13 at 6:30.
The applicant was given homework: revise the town forest access, get Conservation Commission comments, meet abutters on buffers, and send peer review responses.
Residents raised drainage, traffic, school impact, blasting and the form of the town forest access strip, whether a deeded strip or an easement.
A motion not to support Article 40 was first withdrawn so public comment could be taken, then the hearing was closed.

why_it_matters: Article 40 goes to Town Meeting with a Planning Board recommendation against it, so residents will be asked to vote on it with that advice in hand.

The Arrow Estates subdivisions are still under review, and the open questions on drainage, traffic, school impact and road acceptance bear on future road maintenance costs paid from the town budget, mostly taxes.
